paper.title: Can Women Have Children and a Career? IV Evidence from IVF Treatments
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement beyond: 'Data in this article are, in part, taken from IVF registers, held by the Danish National Board of Health (DNBH). …

registers.name_in_paper: IVF register (held by the Danish National Board of Health)
registers.years: 1994-2005 (mandatory reporting; the analysis sample starts with first treatments in 1995)
registers.role: source of the instrument and of the fertility treatment information
variables_mentioned: number of eggs retrieved from the womb
number of fertilized eggs transferred back
treatment outcome (birth, abortion, stillbirth, or failure)
annual earnings (including parental leave and sickness benefits)

registers.name_in_paper: administrative registers matched at Statistics Denmark (demographics)

linkages: The IVF register has been merged at Statistics Denmark to other administrative registers to get longitudinal information running from 1991 to 2009 on demographic and labor market variables; partners of IVF treated women are linked for partner earnings, and matched employer-employee data provide workplace and occupation characteristics.

sample.universe: all IVF treatments in public and private fertility clinics and hospitals in Denmark 1994-2005 (31,666 women receiving 96,807 IVF treatments)
sample.unit_of_observation: woman entering her first IVF treatment with embryo implants
selection_rules: childless women in their first IVF treatment with embryo implants
restricted to women who began their first treatment in 1995 or later (removes 2,908 women treated in 1994)
removes 5,674 women who enter the first IVF treatment with children
removes 4,286 women who had no eggs inserted (failed egg production or failed fertilization)
removes 260 women who could not be matched to the other registers
sample.period: first IVF treatments 1995-2005; register information 1991-2009; women followed up to ten years after (potential) childbirth

construction_notes: All earnings and wage variables are measured in 2008 Danish Kroner. The year of potential childbirth (t = 0) is calculated by adding nine months to the day embryos are transferred. Posttreatment outcomes are constructed as outcome averages over years 0 to 1 (short run), 2 to 5 (medium run) and 6 to 10 (long run); the pretreatment baseline mean is the outcome average over the four years prior to treatment entry (years 1-4 before the first IVF treatment). A 30 percent representative comparison sample of 103,826 women who had their first child between 1995 and 2005 is also used.
